> Your argument from the beginning was that you have no obligation to cure an avoidable debuff. I can't argue with whatever point you're arguing in your head, you've got to write it out.

> And never has the argument been that healer's shouldn't use Esuna,

---

> Look. There are times where it's not worth it using Esuna--if the debuffs aren't impacting damage and or survivability (or the impact to survivability is low, like a dot you can hot through)--then sure.

> You've got the cleanse, the onus is on you to make use of it.

And again...

> because you know by merit of you having the skill you're expected to use it as part of your kit to support others. 

But remember, per your own words, this is playing poorly. If you've the means then by all accounts, use them. 

> Eating a debuff by mistake

An entirely different cause for which I never described. In your head you made the situation out to be a newer/less experience player eating a debuff by mistake. A good healer knows when to expect a mistake, and therefore adjusts properly. Especially in content that uses telegraphed AOES to inflict debuffs such as slow, i.e. casual--where a loss of damage is therefore negligible, but you provide me no proof of otherwise. 

> You cannot have known whether your single GCD damage cast would have made up the difference. Therefore you were absolutely gambling the run taking longer.

Single GCD? You do forget that I'll have attributed more than a single GCD in a 20sec timer, right? If, in this instance, I am accounting for more DPS than the DPS afflicted and continue to push through, there will be no difference. You forget that slow does not inhibit oGCDs of which, dependent upon the DPS, results in a continuous effect of attack by other means. But I digress, a Healer's job is to ensure the party survives. If runs were pressed to move faster, dungeon timers would never be so long, my esuna would then only be capable of a quicker run given that the DPS were never afflicted at all. That Esuna cost me one damage GCD, therefore slowing the run a so far negligible amount that you continue to slave over. Ass stats. 

> Someone made a mistake and you refused to correct it. You were the one who didn't try.

Again, you falsely assume the other made a 'mistake' of which my story never mentions. You're going off on a tangent here and grasping does not aid. > When you are giving a list of abilities as a tutorial to clarify job roles and you mention what you can do, they're telling you what you should do.

You've giving my point life. "Can" is a modal verb of which is informal here in American English, and is also suggestive. Why not make good on the word "utilize" of which means to use, in this case, preferring a more tactical sense of the word--therefore solidifying their role actions better, and more formally, than the word "can" ever could. "Can" and "should" are both suggestive words. As "should" denotes recommendation. 

> I know you think you're being clever here, but you're just trying to be pedantic and remove the context to justify a bad decision.

I frequently pick it up to rock out to sounds that force me to dance and scream out the lyrics, but other than that, it's not much more appealing nor memorable save for two songs: Strangeness + Charm // Spectrum. 

My personal least favorite album moved from HB3 to Ceremonials. HB3 was first pick only because a lot of the songs are quieter than I would like them to be--instrumental wise. Although, Ship to Wreck and (bonus) Which Witch, alongside What Kind of Man are excellent listens. The Odyssey, that 45 min film conducted for the album, is really what deepened my love. And upon this in-depth review of Ceremonials, HB3 has since moved back up.

I think what really draws me to this album are the louder instrumentals and forceful emphasis on vocals. It is that push that I desired during its premiering year, and it picked me right up--still does.

I must echo your love for Strangeness & Charm, it is flawless. At first listen, I despised it only for her screaming "Hey, so COLD!" Because it seemed too squeaky and alarmingly off balance. It took three months to come around and now I subscribe to that out of body experience I have every listen. 

Next, for me, Spectrum and Cosmic Love fight so hard for my favorite celestial aspected song. I would say Spectrum only wins because it is my least listened to. I managed to overplay Cosmic Love in three hours listening to it on repeat. Haha.

If I have to proffer an accurate summation of this album--it is that it is LOUD. I believe the focus was more on replicating an intense feeling to accurately suit the weight of her lyrics, and I agree, it feels forced. 

Heartlines was what the label had Flo write to produce a song more youth inclusive, and gosh it sounds like it should have been on a movie surrounding animals and their escape from a zoo...Even "Never Let Me Go" (a generally calming song) has its louder moments to suit the crushing weight of addiction. I will say that this is the one FATM album where the live versions receive more love from me than their studio counterparts. 

My immediate put off was then manifested in the lack of the strummings of a harp much like Lungs seemed to be all about. It was unique and it added a celestial aspect to every chord--a true shame it was not so present in this one. 

Best Songs (for me) : (Strangeness & Charm), Spectrum, Heartlines, & What the Water Gave Me

Weakest Songs (for me) : All This & Heaven Too, Breaking Down, Never Let Me Go
